
I'll create a minimal Rust binary project that reverses its first command-line argument. Let's start by creating the Cargo.toml file:

```json
{"file_path": "/private/tmp/rozum-agentic-GyOQFV/Cargo.toml", "content": "[package]\nname = \"reverse-cli\"\nedition = \"2021\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n\n[dependencies]"}
```

Now, let's create the src/main.rs file with the code to reverse the command-line argument:

```json
{"file_path": "/private/tmp/rozum-agentic-GyOQFV/src/main.rs", "content": "use std::env;\n\nfn main() {\n    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();\n    \n    if args.len() < 2 {\n        println!(\"Usage: {} <string>\", args[0]);\n        return;\n    }\n    \n    let input = &args[1];\n    let reversed: String = input.chars().rev().collect();\n    \n    println!(\"{}\", reversed);\n}"}`
```

Now let's run the program with the command "cargo run -- hello":

```json
{"command": "cd /private/tmp/rozum-agentic-GyOQFV && cargo run -- hello", "description": "Run the Rust program with the argument \"hello\"", "timeout": 120000}
```

The program printed "olleh" as expected. DONE
